01
Returned error
After a reattachment is accepted, a failing completion now exposes that attempt’s error. Before, the first connection error survived both reattachment failure paths.
Unexplained
This consequence of the loop rewrite is absent from the PR’s stated decisions.
+
02
Fixture translations
Test adapters reinterpret old knobs: client inline=0 becomes 64 KiB, the client directory is precreated, and workspace memoryCapBytes is accepted but unused. Other spill fixtures change thresholds and record splits.
Unexplained
Adapters are stated; these particular translations and their changed exercise of storage paths are unexplained.
+
03
Test oracles
The old resource-policy test block is deleted. Package policy checks already existed. Logger / spool / lifetime expectations now read the policy; added tests exercise selected consumer overrides, retry counts, and timeout purposes.
Unexplained
No specific reason is recorded for deleting that block or changing these expectation sources.
+
04
Required inputs
DaemonPolicy already owns the defaults and crosses process / worker boundaries. This PR replaces consumer-local defaults and optional threshold options with required sections; implementations stay in apps/cli.
Stated
PR: omitted composition must not recreate local defaults.
+
05
Response deadlines
Composition purpose selects 100 ms for a status observer and 250 ms for ordinary lifecycle / execution-status exchanges. Execute admission stays 5 s; acceptance clears that timer.
Stated
PR: status observation and ordinary execution-status requests have distinct deadlines.
+
06
Recovery scopes
Numeric counters replace fixed recovery control flow: 1 execution reattachment per call; 1 fetch-resume allowance inside each execute attempt. A failed fetch feeds completion failure; a reattachment gets a fresh allowance.
Stated
PR: each reattached execute attempt needs its own fetch-resume allowance.
+
07
Output + framing
Capture, spool, disk decoding, socket codec, and both worker-side checks share the output slice: 64 KiB chunks / 256 KiB inline / 256 MiB result / 512 MiB aggregate. Control caps stay 8 MiB JSON / 256 KiB execution control.
Stated
PR + policy record: require the slice throughout the bounded output path.
+
08
Memory + supervision
Delete DaemonResourcePolicy and the second memory-cap input. Use the snapshot’s RSS / worker-heap thresholds for supervision, launch, and reporting; retain 250 ms supervision / 25 ms heap samples / 2 replacements in 10 min, then drain.
Stated
Policy record: one derivation, resource shedding before replacement, and a bounded replacement circuit.
+
09
Startup + shutdown
Required slices preserve coordination, heartbeats, polls, stop escalation, idle lifetime, and drain acknowledgement timings. Startup child-failure retry becomes numeric (default 1). The unused healthy-startup timeout option disappears; healthy warm-up remains unbounded.
Stated
Policy record: preserve distinct cadences and deadlines; progressing warm-up has no project-size deadline.
+
10
Diagnostics
Logger rotation, queue capacity, and disconnected-trace retention now use policy: 10 MiB / 4 backups / 1,024 queued events / 5 min / 1,024 traces (effective trace minimum 1). Trace expiry remains separate from result retention.
Stated
Policy record: bound diagnostic storage and memory while retaining reconnect evidence.
+
11
Test-only bridge
7 new shared adapters (plus local logger / spool wrappers) translate legacy test inputs into policy-backed constructors. Unit tests, e2e helpers, cleanup, and the benchmark switch imports. Production gets no compatibility overloads.
Stated
PR: tests need small thresholds without restoring runtime tuning seams.
+
12
Enforcement boundary
The meta-test expands its retired-name / signature scan across CLI production sources. It catches listed defaults and bypasses. The existing registry grace argument and transport write-chunk option remain; codecs still take required projected numbers.
Stated
Central ownership is stated. Retaining those two optional numeric seams is unexplained in the supplied material.
+

controls.text:
01
Returned error
After a reattachment is accepted, a failing completion now exposes that attempt’s error. Before, the first connection error survived both reattachment failure paths.
Unexplained
This consequence of the loop rewrite is absent from the PR’s stated decisions.
+

02
Fixture translations
Test adapters reinterpret old knobs: client inline=0 becomes 64 KiB, the client directory is precreated, and workspace memoryCapBytes is accepted but unused. Other spill fixtures change thresholds and record splits.
Unexplained
Adapters are stated; these particular translations and their changed exercise of storage paths are unexplained.
+

03
Test oracles
The old resource-policy test block is deleted. Package policy checks already existed. Logger / spool / lifetime expectations now read the policy; added tests exercise selected consumer overrides, retry counts, and timeout purposes.
Unexplained
No specific reason is recorded for deleting that block or changing these expectation sources.
+

04
Required inputs
DaemonPolicy already owns the defaults and crosses process / worker boundaries. This PR replaces consumer-local defaults and optional threshold options with required sections; implementations stay in apps/cli.
Stated
PR: omitted composition must not recreate local defaults.
+

05
Response deadlines
Composition purpose selects 100 ms for a status observer and 250 ms for ordinary lifecycle / execution-status exchanges. Execute admission stays 5 s; acceptance clears that timer.
Stated
PR: status observation and ordinary execution-status requests have distinct deadlines.
+

06
Recovery scopes
Numeric counters replace fixed recovery control flow: 1 execution reattachment per call; 1 fetch-resume allowance inside each execute attempt. A failed fetch feeds completion failure; a reattachment gets a fresh allowance.
Stated
PR: each reattached execute attempt needs its own fetch-resume allowance.
+

07
Output + framing
Capture, spool, disk decoding, socket codec, and both worker-side checks share the output slice: 64 KiB chunks / 256 KiB inline / 256 MiB result / 512 MiB aggregate. Control caps stay 8 MiB JSON / 256 KiB execution control.
Stated
PR + policy record: require the slice throughout the bounded output path.
+

08
Memory + supervision
Delete DaemonResourcePolicy and the second memory-cap input. Use the snapshot’s RSS / worker-heap thresholds for supervision, launch, and reporting; retain 250 ms supervision / 25 ms heap samples / 2 replacements in 10 min, then drain.
Stated
Policy record: one derivation, resource shedding before replacement, and a bounded replacement circuit.
+

09
Startup + shutdown
Required slices preserve coordination, heartbeats, polls, stop escalation, idle lifetime, and drain acknowledgement timings. Startup child-failure retry becomes numeric (default 1). The unused healthy-startup timeout option disappears; healthy warm-up remains unbounded.
Stated
Policy record: preserve distinct cadences and deadlines; progressing warm-up has no project-size deadline.
+

10
Diagnostics
Logger rotation, queue capacity, and disconnected-trace retention now use policy: 10 MiB / 4 backups / 1,024 queued events / 5 min / 1,024 traces (effective trace minimum 1). Trace expiry remains separate from result retention.
Stated
Policy record: bound diagnostic storage and memory while retaining reconnect evidence.
+

11
Test-only bridge
7 new shared adapters (plus local logger / spool wrappers) translate legacy test inputs into policy-backed constructors. Unit tests, e2e helpers, cleanup, and the benchmark switch imports. Production gets no compatibility overloads.
Stated
PR: tests need small thresholds without restoring runtime tuning seams.
+

12
Enforcement boundary
The meta-test expands its retired-name / signature scan across CLI production sources. It catches listed defaults and bypasses. The existing registry grace argument and transport write-chunk option remain; codecs still take required projected numbers.
Stated
Central ownership is stated. Retaining those two optional numeric seams is unexplained in the supplied material.
+
